name: MAFW (Multi-modal Affective Facial expressions in the Wild)
authors_or_creators: Yuanyuan Liu, Wei Dai, Chuanxu Feng, Wenbin Wang, Guanghao Yin, Jiabei Zeng, Shiguang Shan. Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications (BUPT) and Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences.
paper_link: https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3503161.3548190 (ACM MM 2022); extended journal version at IEEE TPAMI 2023
label_taxonomy: mixed: 11 single-emotion classes (anger, disgust, fear, happiness, neutral, sadness, surprise, contempt, anxiety, helplessness, disappointment) + 32 compound-emotion classes; each clip additionally annotated with bilingual (Chinese + English) free-text emotion captions describing facial expression and emotional cause.
license: research-only; access requires signing an End User License Agreement (EULA) via the official site.
known_issues: Heavy class imbalance: the 11 single-emotion classes are dominated by happiness/neutral/sadness/anger while contempt, helplessness, disappointment, and most of the 32 compound classes are rare, making evaluation of compound emotions very low-shot. Clips are sourced from movies, TV dramas, and short videos (predominantly Chinese-language and Hollywood content), so cultural/linguistic bias skews Chinese + Western. Annotation is performed by 11 trained annotators with majority voting; subjective compound-emotion labels still suffer from inter-annotator disagreement. Faces of well-known actors recur across clips, raising potential identity leakage between train and test for subject-dependent evaluation. Audio track is included (multi-modal), but background music/non-speech audio can bias audio-visual models. EULA-restricted, so redistribution is prohibited.
modality: audio-visual (also provides bilingual text captions, so effectively multimodal-text)
annotation_method: expert (11 trained annotators per clip with majority voting); captions written by trained annotators in both Chinese and English
resolution_or_fps: Clips are ~1-10 seconds; original frame rate ~30 fps; resolution varies by source video, faces cropped/aligned for benchmark use. [uncertain]
train_val_test_split: Official 5-fold subject-independent cross-validation protocol for both the 11-class single-emotion task and the 43-class (11+32) compound task. Reported metrics are UAR (unweighted average recall) and WAR (weighted average recall) averaged over the 5 folds.
demographic_metadata: Source clips drawn primarily from Chinese and English/Hollywood movies and TV; gender roughly balanced; no fine-grained age or ethnicity statistics officially released. Predominantly East Asian and Caucasian subjects. [uncertain on exact distribution]
top_sota_model: On the 11-class single-emotion task, recent methods such as MAE-DFER, SVFAP, HiCMAE, FineCLIPER, and Emotion-LLaMA report UAR in the ~42-48% range and WAR in the ~54-60% range. HiCMAE and Emotion-LLaMA (audio-visual / MLLM-based) are among the strongest as of 2024-2025. [uncertain on exact current SOTA]
